title: Tokenized Reward Systems for Federated Learning: The Privacy vs. Fairness Tradeoff
venue: arXiv preprint
read: Supplied PDF in full; equations and result tables visually checked.
problem: Quality disclosure and threshold proofs create different reward incentives.
method: Compares public cosine quality with a threshold-gated reward contract and analyzes noise self-inclusion.
data: MNIST with heterogeneous clients, free-riders and local contract execution.
finding: Reports increasing noise rewards during convergence and higher adversary capture under its threshold allocation.
missing: Does not test its proposed excluding-reference, history and slashing mitigations against poisoning or honest DP noise; uses a verifier stub.
use: Reproduction target and motivating failure mechanism. Published figures are comparison data, not our results.

title: Decentral and Incentivized Federated Learning Frameworks: A Systematic Literature Review
venue: IEEE Internet of Things Journal
read: Abstract, systematic-review procedure, evaluation criteria and future-research sections; journal metadata cross-checked with DBLP.
problem: Decentralized incentive frameworks lack comparable implementation and evaluation evidence.
method: Systematic search and screening with a taxonomy of blockchain, incentive and learning choices.
data: Published federated-learning frameworks, rather than a newly trained benchmark.
finding: Identifies incomplete performance evaluation and scalability analysis as recurring gaps.
missing: Does not experimentally resolve the later cosine self-inclusion problem.
use: Motivates common-update comparisons and reporting computation and settlement costs together.

title: Free-rider Attacks on Model Aggregation in Federated Learning
venue: AISTATS, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research
read: Publisher abstract and BibTeX; PDF attack model, experimental methods, results and discussion.
problem: Clients can acquire the global model without supplying useful local training.
method: Analyzes unchanged-model and stochastically disguised updates under model averaging, including decaying perturbations.
data: MNIST, CIFAR-10 and Shakespeare under FedAvg and FedProx.
finding: Free-riders can obtain comparable final models while slowing convergence, especially at high participation fractions.
missing: Does not measure token capture or implement stake penalties and vesting.
use: Separates model-access free-riding from token extraction; motivates adaptive-noise attacks as a limitation of fixed-noise experiments.

title: Gradient-Driven Rewards to Guarantee Fairness in Collaborative Machine Learning
authors: Xu, Lyu, Ma, Miao, Foo, Low
venue: NeurIPS
read: Publisher abstract; PDF valuation, approximation, reputation, gradient-reward equations and experimental results.
problem: Contribution rewards should distinguish update quality without an auxiliary validation dataset.
method: Defines cosine coalition value, approximates its Shapley allocation, smooths contributions and rewards clients with differently sparsified global gradients.
data: MNIST, CIFAR-10, movie reviews and Stanford sentiment data.
finding: Reports competitive predictive performance and contribution-sensitive gradient rewards.
missing: Original rewards are gradients, not transferable tokens; an on-chain shadow allocation is an adaptation and cannot inherit its training guarantee automatically.
use: Extension rule and a test of self-inclusion under normalized, reputation-weighted references.

title: A Reputation Mechanism Is All You Need: Collaborative Fairness and Adversarial Robustness in Federated Learning
venue: FL-ICML workshop; arXiv version
read: Abstract, algorithm, reputation equations, data and attack settings, result tables and limitations.
problem: Equal global-model access gives weak incentives and permits malicious contributions.
method: Uses normalized reputation-weighted aggregation, cosine-based moving reputation, permanent removal and gradient-download quotas.
data: Image and sentiment benchmarks, with free-riders and several poisoning transformations.
finding: Reports strong accuracy and robustness in its tested settings; identifies difficulty separating similar honest and malicious gradients.
missing: Does not evaluate exact token settlement or the false penalties caused by honest client-level DP noise.
use: Extension comparison; its removal and training feedback must be distinguished from our fixed-trajectory shadow adaptation.

title: Communication-Efficient Learning of Deep Networks from Decentralized Data
venue: AISTATS; PMLR, publisher metadata checked
read: Abstract, local-update/averaging algorithm, experimental setup and communication results opened.
problem: Learning from uneven local data under communication constraints.
method: Sample clients, run local SGD, then combine client models using sample-count weights.
data: MNIST, CIFAR-10, Shakespeare and a large language-modeling task.
finding: More local computation can reduce communication rounds despite heterogeneous data.
missing: Does not design token incentives or establish adversarial reward fairness.
use: Defines the fixed training trajectory; reward rules remain separate.

title: Machine Learning with Adversaries: Byzantine Tolerant Gradient Descent
venue: NeurIPS; publisher BibTeX checked, page range cross-checked with DBLP
read: Abstract, Krum definition, Multi-Krum construction and experimental results opened.
problem: Arbitrary worker updates can defeat linear gradient aggregation.
method: Rank updates by squared distances to nearby peers; Multi-Krum averages a selected subset.
data: MNIST and Spambase; multilayer networks and convolutional experiments.
finding: Neighbor-based selection tolerates tested Byzantine workers, with a speed/robustness tradeoff.
missing: Convergence assumptions do not establish fair token allocation on heterogeneous local-training updates.
use: Acceptance-based payout baseline with the true fault budget supplied; no convergence guarantee claimed for our adaptation.

title: ACE: A Model Poisoning Attack on Contribution Evaluation Methods in Federated Learning
authors: Xu, Jiang, Niu, Jia, Li, and Poovendran
venue: USENIX Security; publisher BibTeX checked
read: Abstract, attack model, model-prediction/error-mitigation method, experimental setup and results opened.
problem: A client can appear valuable without supplying genuinely useful private data.
method: Predict future global updates using historical models and an L-BFGS approximation, with prediction-error filtering and optional amplification.
data: MNIST, CIFAR-10 and Tiny-ImageNet under homogeneous and heterogeneous partitions.
finding: Manipulates contribution rankings across multiple scorers while retaining strong global accuracy.
missing: Does not validate our leave-one-out, EMA and on-chain settlement combination.
use: Bounds our claim: fixed noise/sign/label attacks do not establish robustness against adaptive contribution gaming.

title: Blockchain-based Framework for Scalable and Incentivized Federated Learning
venue: arXiv:2502.14170; matching WWW Companion publication metadata verified in author HTML and DBLP
read: Abstract, architecture, alignment/fairness/consistency formulas, gas evaluation and limitations opened in full-text author HTML. Official arXiv BibTeX export retrieved.
problem: Coordinate FL and incentivize contributions with blockchain transparency and scalable computation.
method: On-chain sample-weighted alignment scores, off-chain cumulative fairness checks and consistency multipliers.
data: Private-chain gas experiments across model-parameter sizes; no measured incentive-fairness experiment in the reported evaluation.
finding: On-chain model computation becomes costly as dimension grows; the paper explicitly leaves incentive effectiveness unevaluated.
missing: No controlled test of self-inclusion bias against the free-rider/poisoning suite or privacy-noise penalty comparison.
use: Closest alignment-and-gas predecessor. Our proposed contribution is the client-excluding reference and controlled common-update evaluation with exact settlement, not the introduction of blockchain rewards or slashing.

title: Defending Against Poisoning Attacks in Federated Learning With Blockchain
authors: Dong, Wang, Sun, Kampffmeyer, Knottenbelt, and Xing
venue: IEEE Transactions on Artificial Intelligence, 5(7):3743--3756; publisher DOI and DBLP metadata checked
read: Author full-text abstract, proposal/voting and asset-redistribution algorithms, experimental setup and results opened; journal metadata verified. Publisher-deposited Crossref BibTeX retrieved after DBLP export was unavailable.
problem: Central aggregation and malicious clients threaten federated model quality.
method: Peer voting decides whether to accept a model; smart contracts redistribute proposer and voter stakes and exclude bankrupt clients.
data: Loan-default prediction on Lending Club, with label-poisoning proposers and malicious voters in a private-chain simulation.
finding: Reported experiments preserve useful training and penalize malicious behavior under the stated voting assumptions.
missing: Does not isolate the direct self-inclusion term in a cosine token scorer or compare the proposed client-excluding rule on identical updates.
use: Prior reward-and-slash defense. Our work tests a particular scoring correction and honest-client costs, rather than claiming slashing itself as novel.

title: Byzantine-Robust Distributed Learning: Towards Optimal Statistical Rates
venue: ICML, PMLR 80:5650--5659; publisher export checked against the paper
read: Abstract, coordinate-wise definitions, statistical assumptions and experimental results opened. Publisher export reverses the name Kannan Ramchandran; corrected against the PDF author line.
problem: Arbitrary worker messages can corrupt distributed empirical-risk minimization.
method: Coordinate-wise median and trimmed-mean gradient aggregation, with statistical-rate bounds and a one-round median alternative.
data: MNIST logistic regression and CNN experiments under reversed or randomized labels, with equal random partitions.
finding: Robust aggregation improves attacked accuracy in the reported experiments; guarantees depend on distributional and loss assumptions.
missing: No heterogeneous local-training token fairness or client-excluding reward reference.
use: Motivates a robust reference building block without transferring its statistical guarantees to our non-IID reward heuristic.

title: FLTrust: Byzantine-robust Federated Learning via Trust Bootstrapping
venue: NDSS 2021; publisher page and DOI checked against publisher-deposited Crossref export
read: Abstract, trust-score equations, Algorithm 2, root-data construction and experimental results opened.
problem: Peer-only aggregation can be manipulated when no update is independently trusted.
method: Score updates by clipped cosine to a server update trained on clean root data; normalize update norms and aggregate by trust.
data: MNIST variants, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, colorectal histology images and human activity recognition, including adaptive attacks.
finding: Reported attacks cause limited degradation when root data is representative; distribution mismatch is an explicit sensitivity.
missing: Requires trusted training examples and measures model robustness rather than token reward fairness.
use: Shows that an independent reference is a distinct trust assumption. Our peer-based exclusion avoids root data but does not inherit this defense guarantee.

title: The Limitations of Federated Learning in Sybil Settings
venue: RAID 2020:301--316; publisher BibTeX and PDF checked
read: Abstract, similarity/history/pardoning algorithm, dataset setup, attack results and false-positive discussion opened.
problem: Coordinated Sybils can overwhelm aggregation methods with bounded Byzantine assumptions.
method: FoolsGold lowers client learning rates using similarity of historical updates on indicative features, with pardoning and a logit transform.
data: MNIST, VGGFace2, KDDCup and Amazon text classification under Sybil poisoning.
finding: Reduces coordinated attacks in tested settings; a single malicious client and similar honest data expose limitations.
missing: No token settlement or direct analysis of a client appearing inside its own aggregate reward reference.
use: Distinguishes peer-to-peer similarity detection from aggregate-alignment rewards and motivates explicit honest false-penalty measurements.

title: Flower: A Friendly Federated Learning Research Framework
venue: arXiv:2007.14390v5, revised 2022; first submitted 2020
read: Abstract, architecture and virtual-client engine, scalability, single-machine and heterogeneous-device experiments opened. Official arXiv BibTeX retrieved: its metadata title includes Research, while the revised PDF heading omits that word. The export's revised year and full author list are retained.
problem: Simulation and real-device FL research require a shared framework across heterogeneous hardware and software.
method: Separate orchestration from client computation, with resource-aware virtual clients and device-independent messages.
data: Amazon book ratings, FEMNIST, RealWorld activity recognition and CIFAR-10 device experiments.
finding: Demonstrates large client populations and heterogeneous deployments; scheduling overhead depends on workload size.
missing: Does not establish reward fairness or reproduce the later Message API's behavior and performance.
use: Framework provenance. Our pinned implementation and measured runtime remain necessary for the actual experiments.

title: Learning Differentially Private Recurrent Language Models
authors: H. Brendan McMahan, Daniel Ramage, Kunal Talwar, and Li Zhang
venue: ICLR 2018; camera-ready arXiv version and DBLP conference metadata checked
read: Abstract, user adjacency, Algorithm 1, clipping/sensitivity, accounting and experimental results opened. Official arXiv BibTeX retrieved; conference identified in the PDF header and DBLP.
problem: Language models can disclose a user's data even when raw training examples are not released.
method: Bound per-user updates, sample users independently and add Gaussian noise to their aggregate; compose privacy loss with a moments accountant.
data: Public Reddit posts grouped by user, with recurrent next-word models.
finding: Large user cohorts permit useful privacy-accuracy tradeoffs at substantial additional computational cost.
missing: Does not protect individually disclosed unnoised updates or test how reward scoring treats honest noised clients.
use: Distinguishes aggregate-release user privacy from our planned client-update release. Sampling, adjacency and the observer must match the accountant.

title: Rényi Differential Privacy
venue: IEEE Computer Security Foundations Symposium, 263--275; publisher DOI and DBLP verified
read: Abstract, RDP definition, adaptive composition, conversion to approximate DP, Gaussian mechanism and numerical comparisons opened. Publisher-deposited Crossref BibTeX retrieved after DBLP export returned a challenge page.
problem: Repeated heterogeneous private computations require composable privacy guarantees.
method: Track Rényi divergence over orders, add privacy curves under composition, and convert the result to an epsilon/delta bound.
data: Theoretical analysis and numerical comparisons of randomized-response, Laplace and Gaussian mechanisms.
finding: Mechanism-specific curves can yield tighter accounting than generic composition bounds.
missing: A privacy definition alone neither bounds an unclipped query nor supplies sampling amplification for an arbitrary disclosure process.
use: Basis for the planned accountant and for explicitly stating sensitivity, adjacency, disclosure and composition assumptions.

title: Fashion-MNIST: a Novel Image Dataset for Benchmarking Machine Learning Algorithms
authors: Han Xiao, Kashif Rasul, and Roland Vollgraf
venue: arXiv:1708.07747v2; official citation export verified
read: Abstract, image-conversion pipeline, label and split construction, and classifier benchmark table opened; official arXiv BibTeX checked.
problem: Digit classification is a limited test of generalization for new learning methods.
method: Construct a clothing-image benchmark with the same input format and split sizes as MNIST.
data: Zalando product photographs converted to grayscale, with silhouette labels and balanced classes.
finding: The supplied classifiers generally perform worse on clothing images than on digits despite compatible input formats.
missing: No federated partition, adversarial reward analysis or privacy guarantee.
use: A second task for the headline reward comparison while retaining the architecture; it does not establish broad real-world generalization.

title: Deep Leakage from Gradients
authors: Ligeng Zhu, Zhijian Liu, and Song Han
venue: NeurIPS 2019; publisher export checked, pages verified against DBLP
read: Abstract, gradient-matching objective and Algorithm 1, image/text experiments, batch sensitivity and defense experiments opened; publisher BibTeX retrieved.
problem: Sharing gradients can disclose the private examples that produced them.
method: Optimize dummy inputs and labels until their gradients match observed gradients for known model weights.
data: MNIST, CIFAR-100, SVHN, LFW and masked-language examples; modified smooth image models.
finding: Demonstrates detailed reconstruction in tested settings; larger batches and sufficient perturbation make recovery harder.
missing: Does not establish reconstruction success for our multi-epoch model differences or prove privacy from a failed attack.
use: Prevents treating local data retention, update hashes or noise without an accountant as a privacy guarantee.

title: A Little Is Enough: Circumventing Defenses For Distributed Learning
venue: NeurIPS 2019; publisher metadata and export verified
read: Abstract, threat model, variance-based perturbation and backdoor algorithms, experimental setup and result tables opened. Publisher export author order retained; the PDF reverses the first two authors.
problem: Outlier-rejection defenses may accept coordinated perturbations that stay within ordinary worker variation.
method: Estimate coordinate means and deviations from corrupted workers, then construct bounded coordinated shifts or backdoor updates.
data: MNIST, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 distributed learning with colluding non-omniscient workers.
finding: Krum, trimmed mean and Bulyan can select harmful updates within the tested perturbation range.
missing: Does not measure our token allocation or certify attacks against every heterogeneous FL reference.
use: Limits the interpretation of simple sign/noise tests and of a median reference: statistical proximity is not evidence of honest computation.

title: Practical Secure Aggregation for Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning
venue: ACM CCS 2017:1175--1191; publisher-deposited Crossref export and PDF checked
read: Abstract, pairwise/double masking and dropout recovery, full protocol, performance analysis, prototype results and input-validity limitations opened.
problem: A server should aggregate client vectors without learning individual contributions, despite client dropout.
method: Pairwise pseudorandom masks, threshold-shared recovery secrets and consistency checks reveal a sum under stated trust thresholds.
data: Java prototype with synthetic vectors, varying client pools and dropouts, plus wide-area execution.
finding: Vector costs amortize communication; dropout recovery increases server work substantially.
missing: Does not validate update quality or provide per-client scores from an aggregate-only interface.
use: Marks an explicit trust boundary: our scorer needs individual updates, so ordinary secure summation cannot be added without redesigning scoring.

title: Free-riders in Federated Learning: Attacks and Defenses
venue: arXiv:1911.12560; official arXiv BibTeX export retrieved
read: Author PDF abstract, attack assumptions, random and delta-report attacks, STD-DAGMM design, MNIST setup and detection results opened. Official arXiv metadata checked.
problem: Participants can obtain the shared model without useful local training.
method: Random and historical-difference reports; an autoencoder detector augmented with update standard deviation.
data: MNIST with fully connected networks, differing client distributions and attacker populations.
finding: The augmented detector improves detection, but overlapping score distributions remain under heavier contamination.
missing: Does not measure cosine-token allocation or exact reward-contract settlement.
use: Earlier free-rider threat and detection baseline; removing self-reference is a different, scale-invariant scoring intervention.

title: A Blockchain-Empowered Incentive Mechanism for Cross-Silo Federated Learning
venue: IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing, 23(10):9240--9253; DBLP and publisher-deposited Crossref export checked
read: Author PDF abstract, resource-capacity mechanism, message updates, transfer minimization, MNIST-calibrated simulations and Ethereum testbed results opened.
problem: Mutually distrusting organizations underprovide training resources.
method: Distributed message updates determine processing capacities and budget-balanced transfers; another algorithm reduces payment transactions.
data: MNIST-calibrated utility simulations and a Python/Solidity Ethereum testbed.
finding: Reported experiments attain the modeled efficient allocation and reduce iterative or transaction costs.
missing: Free-riding means underprovided processing capacity, rather than fabricated update alignment in a token scorer.
use: Prior decentralized incentive and gas work; our comparison isolates reward-reference bias under common updates.
